[curious, lively explainer, warm bright timbre, neutral American accent, conversational pace, starts speaking immediately] This woman could not stop dancing. Not for hours. For days. It was Strasbourg, in the summer of fifteen eighteen. Within a week, dozens of strangers had joined her. By the end of summer, some accounts say hundreds were dancing. So the town leaders made a strange call. More dancing would cure it, they said. They built a stage and hired musicians. It only got worse. Dancers collapsed in the heat, and historians still argue over how many of them actually died. The leading theory: mass panic in a town crushed by famine and disease. And it all started with one woman, dancing.
